info.name: Myrtle — Corporate Account API
info.description:
Every corporate account endpoint: the onboarding flow, the read endpoints that return what was submitted, and what comes after the account exists.

**Folder 1 — Flow A** creates a corporate account. Run it top to bottom: start → validate-otp → basic-details → validate-bvn → kyb → memart → directors → credentials → complete. Each form page is a POST to submit it and a GET (`…r` requests) to read back what was submitted. The read paths mirror the POST paths, with one exception: the BVN page submits at `POST /validate-bvn` but reads at `GET /bvn-data`.

**Folder 2 — Read the submission** returns every page at once: `/submission` grouped by page, `/preview` as one flat record.

**Folder 3 — Flow B** adds another login (max 5 per company) to an account created by Flow A.

**Folder 4 — After onboarding**: login, and one endpoint that demonstrates what corporate users are blocked from.

**Auth model**
- Onboarding token (captured from `validate-otp` as `data.token`, valid 3 days) → `Authorization: Bearer` on every request in folders 1 and 2.
- Lookup token (folder 3, valid 15 minutes) → in the request BODY of create-user, never as a header.
- Session token (from complete / create-user / login, valid 3 days) → normal app use.

**Before you start**
1. Set `baseUrl` (defaults to localhost:8080).
2. Set `email` to an address you can actually receive mail at — A0a and B2 send a real OTP.
3. Set `bvn` and `rcNumber` to values your QoreID/CAC environment will accept.

**Manual steps**: the OTP arrives by email, so paste it into the `otp` variable before running A0b, and into `newUserOtp` before B3. Tokens and references are captured into collection variables automatically; everything else chains.

request.description:
Page 8. Creates the MyWealth corporate client, its investment account and the representative's login. No body.

**Retrying is always safe** — upstream ids are checkpointed as they are created, so a retry resumes rather than creating a second client. The returned token is a normal session token; the onboarding token is now spent and the read endpoints start returning 404.

request.description:
**Everything submitted so far, grouped by the page that collected it** — one call instead of the six per-page reads. Use it to hydrate the whole wizard on entry, and for the review screen.

Adds two things the per-page reads don't have: `nextPage` (the resume page, recalculated now) and `progress.outstandingSteps` (exactly what `complete` enforces).
